One point off because the shared details.tsx file and the cross-linked Pokémon section keep it from being a pure delete-route-plus-nav-link change.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:28 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL builder, used once at views/components.tsx:25 by the CardList every card list shares
app/src/api.ts:3-5 — API base URL, cache map and freshness window live only here
app/src/data.ts:34-37 — species ordering centralized in allSpecies, reused by home and cardsForPokemon
app/src/views/details.tsx:14 — effect-fallback chain duplicated verbatim at details.tsx:65
app/src/data.ts:103 — card list ordering lives in cardsForPokemon, a second ordering site at views/home.tsx:42
changeability.rationale: The highest-risk fixes (sprite, cache, naming, dex ordering) land in one obvious shared module, and CardList guarantees a card fix covers all four lists. Minor duplicated fallback logic and split ordering decisions keep it from a 5.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:1 — clean layering: api.ts → data.ts → views/, views never import each other's internals
app/src/views/home.tsx:20-27 — homeUrl is the single canonical URL builder used by both pagination links and the HX-Push-Url header
app/src/views/layout.tsx:3-7 — ContextRenderer augmentation, the documented jsxRenderer contract; no ad-hoc render plumbing
app/src/index.tsx:50 — the router knows move-table domain (SORT_KEYS set, dir coercion at lines 64-66)
app/src/index.tsx:34-58 — the loadPokemon→loadMoves sequence is wired three times across three routes
coupling.rationale: Modules meet through narrow exported functions, htmx behaviour lives entirely in server-rendered attributes (no client JS to desync), and state is explicit props. Small tangles: sort semantics leak into the router, and the Pokémon loader wiring is repeated per route.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:91 — cardsForPokemon is parameterized by a note callback, not a boolean flag, and handles the real variation (type/move/ability refs)
app/src/data.ts:88 — Card models variation with optional fields (types, note) instead of parallel components
app/src/views/components.tsx:20-40 — CardList/Section/TypeBadge/Count are the right-grained shared atoms reused across all pages
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:31 vs 173-189 — COLUMNS drives headers and sort keys but the body cells are hardcoded per column, so a different sortable table (e.g. items) would be copied
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation well — cards with optional types/notes, a per-ref note callback, one sort utility — with no flag-parameter creep. The move table is the one stretch-failure: its column abstraction stops at the header row.

findings.issue: MoveTable's COLUMNS config (pokemon.tsx:31) drives the header row and sort keys, but the body renders a fixed set of cells per row, so the abstraction only half-exists; adding or reshaping a column means editing both, and a similar-but-different table must be copied
findings.suggestion: Derive the body cells from the same column list (a per-column value extractor in COLUMNS), or drop COLUMNS and accept the table as a single-purpose component

findings.issue: Loaders and pages for three unrelated resources (moves, abilities, types) share one 'details' grab-bag file, so per-resource changes and removals all touch the same file
findings.suggestion: Split into per-resource files (moves.tsx, abilities.tsx, types.tsx) matching how routes and ownership actually divide

findings.issue: Move-table domain knowledge (valid sort keys, ascending/descending coercion at lines 64-66) lives in the router rather than with the sort code in pokemon.tsx
findings.suggestion: Move sort-key validation and dir coercion into a parseSortQuery helper next to SortKey/SortDir in views/pokemon.tsx

findings.issue: The loadPokemon→notFound→loadMoves sequence is wired identically in three routes, so a change to how a Pokémon page loads data is repeated
findings.suggestion: Extract a small withPokemon(c, name) helper (or middleware) that resolves the data or returns the 404 response

findings.issue: Card list ordering is decided at build time in two places (cardsForPokemon's sort and loadHome's slice at home.tsx:42-48), so a new global card ordering (e.g. sort by name) cannot land in one place
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit ordering option (or sort inside CardList) so ordering has a single home

findings.issue: The effect-fallback chain englishEffect(...) || latestFlavorText(...) || Dash is duplicated verbatim at details.tsx:65
findings.suggestion: Extract a describeEffect(entries, chance?) helper in data.ts

findings.issue: Every new detail page must remember to fetch and thread the typeLabels map through loader and components (details.tsx:107, pokemon.tsx:63, 92)
findings.suggestion: Either fold label lookup into a small typeBadge(name) data helper or accept the boilerplate consciously; a shared helper would make future pages one call instead of three

summary: A cleanly layered little codebase where the risky changes (sprites, caching, naming, card rendering) each land in one obvious shared place, and every Pokémon card list genuinely funnels through one component. The main friction points are the move table's half-finished column abstraction, a three-resource grab-bag views file, and split card-ordering logic. I'd merge it with the low-severity cleanups noted.
